title: Key Word Transformation: Set 3
instructions: For questions 1-6, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

items.sentence1: Whatever method you use, the results will be roughly the same.
items.sentence2Suffix: method you use, the results will be roughly the same.
items.explanation: 'No matter what/how/which' means 'regardless of', and functions like 'whatever' + noun at the start of a sentence.

items.sentence1: If you invest all your savings in a single company, you might lose everything.
items.sentence2Prefix: By investing all your savings in a single company, you
items.explanation: 'Run the risk of doing something' means to expose yourself to a possible negative outcome; 'of' is followed by the gerund.

items.sentence1: She used the quiet afternoon to finish all the paperwork she had been putting off.
items.sentence2Suffix: finish all the paperwork she had been putting off.
items.answer: advantage of the quiet afternoon to
items.explanation: 'Take advantage of something to do something' means to make good use of an opportunity; 'advantage' is the key noun in this fixed pattern.

items.sentence1: He found it extremely hard to concentrate because of the constant noise outside.
items.sentence2Suffix: because of the constant noise outside.
items.explanation: 'Have difficulty doing something' is the fixed pattern (never 'difficulty to do'); 'considerable' intensifies it to match 'extremely hard'.

items.sentence1: Over the years, the company gradually forgot its original mission as it focused on profit.
items.sentence2Prefix: Over the years, the company gradually
items.sentence2Suffix: its original mission as it focused on profit.
items.explanation: 'Lose sight of something' means to forget or stop focusing on an important aim or principle.

items.sentence1: Although his essay was well argued, I could still criticise a few points of grammar.
items.sentence2Prefix: Although his essay was well argued, I could still
items.explanation: 'Find fault with something' means to criticise or point out flaws in it.
